# CCA / C-AIME: Lead-Scientist Brief (merged and adversarially verified)

**Date:** 2026-09-25

**Inputs:** 8 dimensions: citations-core, maia2-lc0, stockfish19, timing-humanbot, gametheory-libs, sota-sweep, neuro-validity and chaos-math. Each has a researcher pass and a verifier pass.

**Status legend:**

| Tag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **V** | Verified: at least one opened URL, carried over from the dimension |
| **C** | Corrected: the spec or an intermediate claim was wrong, and the correction is verified |
| **U** | Unverifiable |
| **D** | Disputed: researcher and verifier disagree and neither gave decisive evidence |
| computed | Sandbox numerics run by the dimensions (Python 3.13.3, numpy 2.1.2, this machine). §6 has the recipe to reproduce them. |
| derived | Team algebra |
| est. | Estimate, not measured |

**Merge rule:** where researcher and verifier disagree, the verifier's version is kept only if the verifier cited evidence. Otherwise the item is marked D.

**Nothing in this brief is legal advice.**

## 0. Executive verdict

1. **The three C-AIME mechanisms have problems.**
   - (1) Virtual neuromodulation is a metaphor. A "cortisol" variable is on the wrong physiological timescale for per-move updates. Rename it `arousal` and validate it against human data.
   - (2) Lorenz modulation of c_puct has nothing to act on, because Stockfish 19 is alpha-beta and has no c_puct. An observer who cannot see the internal state gains no extra unpredictability from chaos compared with a keyed PRNG. Gate it behind an A/B test.
   - (3) The spec's objective is not piKL. Canonical piKL is π ∝ τ·exp(Q/λ).
2. **Highest expected impact:**
   - canonical piKL over a Stockfish-sound candidate set;
   - human-aware expectimax over a Maia reply model;
   - position-difficulty features as the main error signal;
   - a clock-aware timing model.
3. **Install blockers:**
   - `maia2` 0.11.0 requires Python <3.13, and the target machine has 3.13.3.
   - The PyPI torch 2.8.0 Windows wheels are CPU-only.
4. **License:** python-chess is GPL-3.0+, so any distributed CCA build is a GPL combined work. License CCA as GPL-3.0-or-later. If Maia-3 code is imported into a hosted bot, use AGPL-3.0.
5. **Deployment:** Lichess BOT account only. The account must be fresh and the upgrade is irreversible. Any live test against human opponents needs informed consent and an IRB-style ethics review.

### 1.7 Do not cite

- **nexicturbo/Human-Chess-Bot.** An AI-generated repo built in one day. It is anti-cheat-evasion software, and its constants have no sources. Cite Sigman 2010 instead.
- **The "21.26% premoves" figure.** Its only source is a Lichess user blog by oortcloud_o (2023-06-15). The number is the share of moves under 1 s in the eval-annotated subset of 60+0 bullet games, so it is not a premove rate (https://lichess.org/@/oortcloud_o/blog/chess-with-some-data-visualization/oof5Ij1M).
- **Andrews 2021's "category error" argument.** Keep it out until someone reads the paper.

## 2. Owner-spec errata

**Origin tags:**
- **[S]** explicit in the owner spec as given in this task;
- **[C]** a spec claim or citation checked by a dimension;
- **[R]** an intermediate or third-party claim corrected during verification.

| # | Claim | Correction | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| E1 [S] | "piKL" objective π* = argmax E[Q + λH(s')] − KL(π‖P_maia2) | **Not piKL.** piKL (Eq. 5) is maximize E_π[Q] − λ·D_KL(π‖τ) with τ = P_maia2(·\|s, elo), which has the closed form π*(a) ∝ τ(a)·exp(Q(a)/λ). The spec's version has closed form π* ∝ P_maia2·exp(Q + λH(s')) (derived): the KL weight is fixed at 1, and Q and H must be in the same units. No source supports the H(s') term. Rename it "piKL-style with CCA modifications", or switch to the canonical form. With a policy-entropy bonus αH(π) the optimum is π ∝ τ^{λ/(λ+α)}·exp(Q/(λ+α)) (derived and verified). | https://proceedings.mlr.press/v162/jacob22a/jacob22a.pdf |
| E2 [S] | Lorenz RK4 modulates c_puct of the search | Stockfish 19 is alpha-beta and has no c_puct; neither "cpuct" nor "puct" appears in sf_19 `engine.cpp`. The mechanism only applies to lc0 or to CCA's own PUCT search. For Stockfish, see §6.4 for what to modulate instead. | https://raw.githubusercontent.com/official-stockfish/Stockfish/sf_19/src/engine.cpp |
| E3 [C] | λ ∼ c_puct·√N (quoted from piKL's restatement of Grill) | Grill Eq. 4 gives λ_N = c·√(Σn_b)/(\|A\| + Σn_b), which is Õ(1/√N) and shrinks as visits accumulate. Their regularizer is the reverse KL(τ‖π), whose solution is π̄ = λ_N·τ/(α − q), not a softmax. Modules 2 and 3 are therefore analogous but not the same knob (the S13 "redundant" claim is wrong). Allie's decode.py reinstates ~1/√N_sim through `scale_c_puct=True`. | https://arxiv.org/pdf/2007.12509 · https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ippolito-cmu/allie/main/src/evaluation/decode.py |
| E4 [C] | Maia-2 citation | See tang2024maia2 in §1.1. Also delete arXiv 2406.07548. | https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.20553 |
| E5 [C] | "Cornell & Toronto model predicts WHEN humans err from Board Entropy, Time Scarcity, Cognitive fatigue, Confirmation bias" | The papers say otherwise. **AKM 2016** (MSR/Cornell/Harvard) uses three feature groups: skill, time and difficulty. On a balanced blunder set: difficulty 0.75, skill 0.55, time 0.53, and skill and time add nothing once difficulty is included. Their time effect is nonlinear: blunder rate rises sharply below about 10 s and is flat above that. Scope: tablebase positions with at most 6 pieces, from FICS 3-minute games and a GM corpus. **Maia KDD'20 §5** has a blunder CNN at 71.7% on a balanced test set (board plus metadata: ratings, % time remaining, cp). Full-text search: "confirmation" 0 hits, "fatigue" 0, "entropy" 0 (the only entropy is the cross-entropy loss). | https://arxiv.org/pdf/1606.04956 · https://arxiv.org/pdf/2006.01855 |
| E6 [C] | "piKL comes from Cicero" | piKL is from Jacob et al., ICML 2022. Cicero (Science 2022) used it later for planning, through the DiL-piKL code path (`bqre1p_agent.py`, where "bqre1p" is the internal name for DiL-piKL). | https://raw.githubusercontent.com/facebookresearch/diplomacy_cicero/main/README.md |
| E7 [S] | Pick an SF19 Windows asset: x86-64-avxvnni, avx2 or bmi2 | SF19 ships **only universal binaries**. Use `stockfish-windows-x86-64-universal.zip`. It dispatches at runtime: without AVX512F/VL/BW it picks avxvnni if the CPU has it, otherwise bmi2. | https://raw.githubusercontent.com/official-stockfish/Stockfish/sf_19/src/universal/entry_x86.cpp |
| E8 [S] | Win-rate model normalized so that 100 cp = 50% win at move 32 | That was the model only up to SF16.1. From SF17 on, including SF19, it is based on **material** (clamp to [17, 78], anchored at 58). The SF docs text is stale. python-chess `PovScore.wdl()` defaults to the SF16.1 model and is mis-calibrated for SF19. | https://raw.githubusercontent.com/official-stockfish/Stockfish/sf_19/src/uci.cpp |
| E9 [S] | "SF19 NNUE trained via QAT" | Correct. Reword as: "SF19 nets were trained with techniques including QAT (fake quantization in nnue-pytorch `model/quantize.py`)". The engine itself only runs integer SIMD inference. | https://raw.githubusercontent.com/official-stockfish/nnue-pytorch/master/model/quantize.py |
| E10 [S] | Cortisol ODE driven per move by surprise and time pressure | Physiologically implausible at move timescale. Cortisol rises reliably only for uncontrollable or social-evaluative stressors (Dickerson & Kemeny 2004, 208 studies) and peaks about 21–40 min after onset (secondary citation). Fast arousal in chess is measurable, but through the autonomic system (heart rate and HRV: Troubat 2009, Leone 2012). In one chess tournament study, winners had *higher* cortisol than losers (Dovom 2024). Relabel the variable as `arousal`, motivated by LC-NE and pupil-linked arousal. | https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15122924/ |
| E11 [S] | "Shannon surprise", citing Itti & Baldi | −ln p is surprisal (Smith & Levy 2013). Itti & Baldi define Bayesian surprise, KL(posterior‖prior), which is a different quantity. | https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1016/j.visres.2008.09.007 |
| E12 [S] | Surprise under Maia-2 plus time pressure is meaningful in scrambles | Maia-2 was trained on rapid games only. It drops the first 10 plies and every position where the mover had 30 s or less left. It has no clock input and no move history. Its probabilities are therefore out of distribution in scrambles and in the opening. | https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CSSLab/maia2/main/maia2/main.py |
| E13 [S] | Tunnel-vision Gaussian attention mask | The phenomenon is real: Einstellung (Bilalić 2008), Easterbrook's cue utilization, arousal-biased competition. But Einstellung is driven by schemas and plans, and chess chunks are tied to specific squares. **No evidence supports a spatial Gaussian.** "Stress causes Einstellung" has 0 PubMed hits. There is counter-evidence: acute stress *improved* set-shifting (Gabrys 2019), and tonic LC activity is linked to *exploration* (Aston-Jones & Cohen 2005). | https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18565505/ |
| E14 [C] | Stress or time pressure makes players take more risks, so it can be exploited | In chess field data it is the other way round. At the FIDE World Cups 2013–2023, less time led to **more risk-averse** moves, especially when trailing, and risk-taking rose after mistakes (Carow & Witzig 2025; their risk measure is a new ML proxy). Lab gambling meta-analysis: d = .17 (k = 32, N = 1829). | https://api.openalex.org/works/doi:10.1016/j.jebo.2025.107218 |
| E15 [C] | Yerkes–Dodson inverted U | The arousal inverted U is a later reformulation misattributed to Yerkes & Dodson (Teigen 1994), and its supporting evidence is weak (Corbett 2015). | https://api.openalex.org/works/doi:10.1177/0959354394044004 |
| E16 [C] | Lorenz dynamics model human emotion or the temperament of Tal and Dubov | No evidence for either. The best-known Lorenz emotion model (Losada) was **formally withdrawn** in 2013. Status is "unsupported", not "refuted" in general (the verifier's evidence-based downgrade). | https://arxiv.org/pdf/1307.7006 · https://retractionwatch.com/?p=15724 |
| E17 [C] | Working memory is 7±2 chunks | Modern estimate is about 4 (range 3–5; Cowan 2001). In chess, experts use at most about 3 chunks, but a chunk can hold up to 15 pieces (Gobet & Clarkson 2004). | https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1017/S0140525X01003922 |
| E18 [C] | Dopamine drives risk-seeking and pleasure | Only the reward-prediction-error role is solid (Schultz, Dayan & Montague 1997). L-DOPA raised risky choice on gain trials only (Rutledge 2015). "Pleasure" language is pop-neuroscience (Berridge & Robinson 1998). There is no chess evidence. | https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9054347/ |
| E19 [C] | The Free Energy Principle supports the C-AIME mechanisms | The FEP is a framework, not evidence, and its falsifiability is contested. | https://api.openalex.org/works/doi:10.1007/s11229-018-01932-w |
| E20 [C] | A psyche-modulated engine is novel | Ailed (arXiv:2603.05352) is prior art. Its psyche scalar ψ ∈ [−100, 100] reshapes the Maia2 policy. Against Maia2-1100, stress lowered its own score from 50.8% to 30.1%, and it has no human validation. | https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.05352 |
| E21 [C] | Timing constants taken from Human-Chess-Bot: "log-normal SD = a + b·mean", "peak at moves 15–25", "AR(1) ρ = 0.4", "21.26% premoves", "sqrt complexity", "12M Lichess games" | Each is wrong or unsupported. The (a, b) values are Sigman 2010 FICS statistics measured *across games*, used without attribution and misapplied as within-draw spread, which gives CV of about 0.93–1.24 (<1400) and 1.5–3.4 (1900). The move counter counts plies, so the peak is at ply 20, about move 10. The autocorrelation is emergent (lag-1 corr(log T) 0.42–0.49), not a controlled ρ. The 21.26% comes from the bullet blog in §1.7. The "sqrt complexity" is actually a step function. The repo contains no data and never reads the clock. | https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nexicturbo/Human-Chess-Bot/main/src/maia_worker.py |
| E22 [C] | Time pressure is the main driver of human error | Not established. Difficulty dominates in AKM's tablebase positions. The PNAS 2026 paper finds time pressure associated with lower decision quality (elite players, classical time control). Treat both as inputs, with difficulty first-class. Two overreaches are also downgraded: the researcher's "time pressure refuted" and the Human-Chess-Bot review's "time pressure is the most important driver". | https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1073/pnas.2531472123 |
| E23 [C] | KDD'20 is the "25th" SIGKDD; Da Costa et al. is 2021 | It is the 26th. Da Costa et al. is 2020, J Math Psych vol. 99. | Crossref records in §1 |
| E24 [C] | Cicero repo is CC-BY-NC for most files | Code is MIT, except `fairdiplomacy_external/`, which is AGPL-3.0. Only the model weights are CC-BY-NC 4.0. | https://raw.githubusercontent.com/facebookresearch/diplomacy_cicero/main/LICENSE.md |
| E25 [C] | Regan–Haworth is a QRE model for chess | It is a one-sided stochastic choice model, not a logit QRE: y = exp(−(δ/s)^c) and p_i = p_0^{1/y_i}. There is no equilibrium. | https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/download/7951/7810 |
| E26 [C] | pymdp computes EFE as risk + ambiguity | The code computes neg_efe += info_gain + utility − param_info_gain. That equals −(risk + ambiguity) only when C holds normalized log-preferences (derived). | https://raw.githubusercontent.com/infer-actively/pymdp/main/pymdp/control.py |
| E27 [C] | pymdp can model the chess state space | Infeasible. There are about (4.82 ± 0.03)×10^44 legal positions (Tromp). pymdp is only usable for a small latent "psych-state" POMDP. | https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tromp/ChessPositionRanking/main/README.md |
| E28 [R] | Maia-2 Elo buckets are (0,1000], (1000,1100], … (2000,∞) | The shipped code (`utils.py`) has **11 bins**: <1100, 1100–1199, …, 1900–1999, ≥2000. Every Elo below 1100 looks the same to the model, and so does every Elo of 2000 or more. | https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CSSLab/maia2/main/maia2/utils.py |
| E29 [R] | lc0 CPuct defaults 2.15 / 18368 / 2.82 (lczero.org flags page) | That page was last updated in 2020. Current defaults (v0.32.1, v0.33.0-rc0 and master): CPuct 1.745, CPuctBase 38739, CPuctFactor 3.894. | https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LeelaChessZero/lc0/v0.32.1/src/search/classic/params.cc |
| E30 [R] | lc0 `policyhead` search outputs per-move P | It outputs only the argmax bestmove and one info line. | https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LeelaChessZero/lc0/v0.32.1/src/search/instamove/instamove.cc |
| E31 [R] | Maia-3 over UCI can feed KL or surprise terms | Its UCI info lines carry only multipv rank, cp, WDL and pv, with **no probabilities**. Getting P requires importing the code in-process, which brings AGPL obligations. | https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CSSLab/maia3/main/maia3/uci.py |
| E32 [R] | SF19 terminates on any invalid input | It calls exit(1) only on a bad position, FEN or illegal move, an unparsable `go` argument, or flip/perft errors. An unknown command, unknown option, or out-of-range value is **silently ignored**. | https://raw.githubusercontent.com/official-stockfish/Stockfish/sf_19/src/uci.cpp |
| E33 [R] | Hamade: "traps set for 1100 players backfire against 1900 opponents" | The quote is about a mismatched *partner* model in collaborative play, not about opponents. | https://arxiv.org/html/2405.05066v1 |
| E34 [R] | maia2 installs on Python 3.13 | It does not. It declares `requires-python >=3.10,<3.13`. | https://pypi.org/pypi/maia2/json |

## 3. License matrix

**Recommended CCA license: GPL-3.0-or-later.** Use AGPL-3.0 if Maia-3 code is imported into a hosted bot.

**Use modes:**
- *import*: in-process dependency.
- *subprocess*: separate OS process speaking UCI over stdin/stdout. By the FSF's reading this is aggregation, not linking.
- *download-at-install*: fetched from the official upstream, not rehosted.
- *reimplement*: clean-room reimplementation from the paper.
- *must-not-copy*.

| Component (version) | License | How CCA may use it | Notes and evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Stockfish 19 (sf_19) | GPL-3.0-or-later | subprocess + download-at-install | Verify the SHA-256 digest and the immutable-release attestation. If bundling, ship the **unmodified official zip**, which already contains src/ and Copying.txt; pointing to GitHub for source instead leaves CCA responsible if that source ever disappears. Server-side play is not "conveying" (GPLv3 §0). Never rehost a modified binary. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/official-stockfish/Stockfish/sf_19/Copying.txt |
| SF19 `win_rate_params` constants | GPL (source) | reimplement (port) | Fine once CCA is GPL. Add a unit test against the engine's `wdl` output. |
| python-chess, PyPI `chess` 1.11.2 | GPL-3.0+ | import | This makes any distributed CCA a GPL combined work (FSF reading). Depend on `chess`, not the `python-chess` 1.999 stub. https://pypi.org/pypi/chess/json |
| Maia-2, `maia2` 0.11.0 | code MIT (© 2024 CSSLab) | import (needed to get logits) | It depends on `chess` (GPL). https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CSSLab/maia2/main/LICENSE |
| Maia-2 weights (rapid and blitz .pt) | **U**: no separate license | download-at-install (gdown with SHA-256 check) | Do not rehost until the license is clarified. |
| Maia-1, CSSLab/maia-chess (v1.0 .pb.gz) | GPL-3.0 | download-at-install + lc0 subprocess | https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CSSLab/maia-chess/master/LICENSE |
| Maia-3, CSSLab/maia3 (0.1.0, git only) | AGPL-3.0. ## 4. Engineering facts

### 4.1 Environment decision

**Pin the CCA runtime to a uv-managed Python 3.12.** Reasons:
- maia2 requires <3.13 and must run in-process to expose logits.
- open-spiel ships a cp312 win_amd64 wheel.
- lichess-bot requires ≥3.11.
- `chess` requires ≥3.8.
- pymdp pins jax <0.11.1. jax 0.11.0 requires Python ≥3.12. **A jaxlib 0.11.0 cp312 Windows wheel was not explicitly checked**; the check covered cp313 only.

The alternative is a Python 3.13 core with Maia in a separate Python 3.12 worker process connected over IPC.

**Maia install pitfalls:**
- Never let a 3.13 resolver backtrack to maia2 0.10.0. That version has no Requires-Python metadata, hard-pins pyzstd==0.15.9 (no cp313 wheel, so it needs an MSVC build), and also pins torch==2.8.0 and numpy==2.1.3.
- Do not use maia2 0.9.x or 0.1. Those wheels declare no dependencies at all, and 0.9.1 pins torch 2.4.0.
- Forcing 0.11.0 onto 3.13 with `--ignore-requires-python` is technically plausible, because every 0.11.0 dependency has a cp313 Windows wheel. It is unsupported and untested.

**torch:**
- The PyPI torch 2.8.0 win_amd64 wheels are **CPU-only** (about 241 MB, with the nvidia-* dependencies gated to Linux). `device="auto"` then silently falls back to CPU.
- Install from https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128. `torch-2.8.0+cu128` exists for cp312 and cp313 win_amd64; cu126 and cu129 builds also exist.

**Install sequence.** The uv flag syntax below was not re-verified in this review.

```
uv python install 3.12
uv venv --python 3.12 .venv   &&  activate .venv
uv pip install torch==2.8.0 --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128
uv pip install maia2==0.11.0 chess==1.11.2
uv pip install open-spiel==2.0.2          # dev group only; NOT [full] (pygraphviz needs Graphviz C headers)
uv pip install inferactively-pymdp==1.0.4  # optional; CPU JAX only on native Windows
```

In a uv project, pin torch to the cu128 index explicitly in pyproject.

**Windows asyncio:** keep the default ProactorEventLoop. `WindowsSelectorEventLoopPolicy` breaks python-chess engine startup with a NotImplementedError.

### 4.2 Maia-2 API (maia2 0.11.0)

Package details:
- PyPI upload 2026-07-15. Pure-Python wheel built with flit.
- Dependency ranges: chess ≥1.10,<2; einops ≥0.8,<1; gdown ≥5.2.2,<6; numpy ≥2.1.3,<3; pandas ≥2.2.3,<3; pyyaml ≥6.0.2,<7; pyzstd ≥0.19.1,<0.20; requests ≥2.33,<3; torch ≥2.8.0,<2.9; tqdm ≥4.66.3,<5.
- CI runs on ubuntu only, Python 3.10–3.12.

Signatures:
- `maia2.model.from_pretrained(type, device="auto", save_root="./maia2_models") -> MAIA2Model`
  - `type` must be `'rapid'` or `'blitz'`; anything else raises ValueError.
  - `device`: `auto` tries cuda, then mps, then cpu. `cuda[:N]`, `mps`, `cpu` and `gpu` (alias for cuda) are also accepted. RuntimeError if the requested device is unavailable.
  - Loads with `torch.load(map_location='cpu', weights_only=True)`, then `checkpoint['model_state_dict']`.
  - **It print()s two lines to STDOUT and re-hashes the ~267 MB file with SHA-256 on every call.** Redirect stdout during load if the process speaks UCI.
- `maia2.inference.prepare() -> [all_moves_dict, elo_dict, all_moves_dict_reversed]`
- `maia2.inference.inference_each(model, prepared, fen, elo_self, elo_oppo) -> (move_probs, win_prob)`
  - `move_probs`: dict {uci: p} over legal moves only, sorted descending, **each rounded to 4 decimals**. Any P < 5e-5 becomes 0.0.
  - `win_prob`: **White-perspective** expected score, clamp(v/2 + 0.5, 0, 1), rounded to 4 decimals. The README says it is "not a calibrated win probability or the active player's score".
  - `elo_self` is always the side to move.
  - Raises ValueError on a position with no legal moves or an invalid FEN side-to-move field.
- `maia2.inference.inference_batch(data, model, verbose, batch_size, num_workers) -> (data, accuracy)`
  - Required columns: `board`, `move`, `active_elo`, `opponent_elo` (`move` is required even for pure prediction).
  - Adds columns `win_probs` and `move_probs`. Uses `shuffle=False`. Use `num_workers=0` on Windows.
- `MAIA2Model.forward(boards, elos_self, elos_oppo) -> (logits_maia[1880], logits_side_info[2021], logits_value)`
  - The move vocabulary has 1880 entries: 1456 queen-line moves + 336 knight moves + 88 promotions.
  - Call `model.eval()` first, because forward applies dropout.
- `maia2.dataset.load_example_test_dataset(save_root="./maia2_data")` returns a DataFrame filtered to move_ply > 10. `load_example_train_dataset(...)` returns a CSV path.

Model inputs and training data:
- Input is one position encoded as 18×8×8 (12 piece planes, side to move, 4 castling, en passant). No history, no clock. Black-to-move positions are mirrored.
- Elo enters through `nn.Embedding(11, 128)` for self and opponent.
- Config: dim_cnn 256, dim_vit 1024, 5 CNN blocks, 2 ViT blocks, vit_length 8.
- Training: the paper uses Lichess **rapid** games from Jan 2013–Nov 2023 (excluding Dec 2019), 169M games / 9.1B positions. The released presets cover 2018-05..2023-11. First 10 plies dropped. A position is kept only if the mover's clock *after* the move is above 30 s. BOT players are excluded. At most 20 games per (self-bin, opponent-bin) pair per data chunk, so the data is Elo-pair-balanced, not population-weighted.
- Average move-match 53.25%, versus 51.39% for the best Maia-1.

Weights (Google Drive, about 267 MB each):

| Model | Drive id | sha256 |
|---|---|---|
| rapid | `1gbC1-c7c0EQOPPAVpGWubezeEW8grVwc` | `65aae8465eed5e65df66a24ea7370715579f9e5435098d06fe18bdb1e267e997` |
| blitz | `1X-Z4J3PX3MQFJoa8gRt3aL8CIH0PWoyt` | `5090d5d0d49dc29787c08d13febbed5b2da81a18c2ddcd8a90070cd3b43c44b2` |

Pre-cache the weights for CI and offline use.

Known issues:
- GitHub #4 and #5: knight-shuffle loops from the start position.
- GitHub #13: the maiachess.com web model differs from the PyPI package. Benchmark the actual checkpoint rather than trusting web or paper numbers.

Required CCA adapter:
- Signature: `logits(fen, elo_self, elo_oppo) -> (legal_moves, log_probs: float32, value_white)`.
- Reuse the package's own preprocessing, run under `torch.no_grad()`, and take a masked log_softmax.
- Apply an epsilon floor, batch every position of a search in one call, and guard terminal positions.
- For opponent-move surprise, query the position *before* the opponent's move with elo_self = opponent Elo and elo_oppo = CCA's Elo.

### 4.3 Maia-3 (CSSLab/maia3 0.1.0)

- Not on PyPI (404). Install from git and pin a commit hash.
- `requires-python >=3.10`, with no upper cap. Dependencies are unpinned: huggingface-hub ≥0.23, numpy, python-chess, torch. A Python 3.13 install is **untested**.
- HF weights: `UofTCSSLab/Maia3-5M` (20,968,049 B), `-23M` (91,799,307 B), `-79M` (315,651,851 B), plus an ablation model. Trained on Lichess Jan 2023–Jul 2025. Pin the HF repo id and revision; there are two namespaces, UofTCSSLab and MaiaChess.
- CLI `maia3-uci` (aliases maia3-5m, 23m, 79m). UCI options:
  - `Elo`, `SelfElo`, `OppoElo`: spin 0..5000, default Elo 1500. Elo is interpolated continuously between learned embeddings.
  - `Temperature`: default **1.0**, which means stochastic sampling; 0 = argmax.
  - `TopP`.
  - `MultiPV`: default 5, range 1..20.
  - Flags: `--use-uci-history` is **off by default** (history is then padded with the current position), `--history 8`.
  - AMP fp16 autocast is on by default on CUDA. That matters for low-probability logits.
- Info lines carry multipv rank, cp (derived from WDL), WDL and pv, with **no policy probabilities**. The WDL comes from a value head described as "human-game outcome predictions". Its calibration is unverified.
- `include_time_info` exists in the architecture but is False in every released preset, so Maia-3 has no clock input.
- Headline move-matching accuracy is 57.1%. That is a family-level figure for the largest model, not for the 5M model.

### 4.4 Maia-1 through lc0

- Nine nets, `maia-1100` … `maia-1900` in `.pb.gz`, 1.24–1.33 MB each. Download: https://github.com/CSSLab/maia-chess/releases/download/v1.0/maia-<elo>.pb.gz
- To read the policy P: use `classic` search with `go nodes 1`, set `VerboseMoveStats=true` and `PolicyTemperature=1.0` (the default 1.359 flattens P).
- Whether these nets load on lc0 v0.32.x is **U**. The only report is lc0 issue #1920 (Linux, v0.30.0, closed without comment). Test locally.
- Official Lichess BOTs still run Maia-1 only: maia1, maia5, maia9.

### 4.5 Stockfish 19

**Release:**
- Tag `sf_19`, published 2026-09-05T08:33:17Z, commit edb0d9db6731067ec50ce619ff372b463bc4dd5d, Bench 2497913.
- It is a GitHub **Immutable release** with an automatic release attestation. The exact `gh` CLI command to verify the attestation was not confirmed.

**Asset for this machine:**
- File: `stockfish-windows-x86-64-universal.zip`, 81,431,614 B (API figure), digest `sha256:3c8bf1f9ea66a09350a40df4f632288285ac206d99f33ab5842c408fc30b48a7`.
- Download: https://github.com/official-stockfish/Stockfish/releases/download/sf_19/stockfish-windows-x86-64-universal.zip
- Executable inside: `stockfish/stockfish-windows-x86-64-universal.exe`. Built with Mingw-w64 GCC. It contains 8 builds and dispatches at runtime.
- The owner states the CPU has AVX-VNNI, but **Intel ARK lists only SSE4.1/4.2/AVX2** for the i9-14900HX. Confirm on the machine which build was dispatched. Either path runs correctly; the speed difference is unmeasured.

**Engine internals:**
- NNUE: SFNNv16, feature sets HalfKAv2_hm + FullThreats + PP_3Wide, L1 1024 / L2 32 / L3 32, 8 PSQT buckets, 8 layer stacks. Single net `nn-1a298aa575a0.nnue`. The small net and the `EvalFileSmall` option are gone.
- Strength vs SF18: +44.7 Elo single-thread and +39.3 with 8 threads (computed from Fishtest counts, UHO book at 60+0.6). Neither run used the exact release binaries, so quote this as approximately SF19 vs SF18.

**UCI options (name: type default [range]):**

| Option | Type and default | Range / note |
|---|---|---|
| Debug Log File | string "" | |
| NumaPolicy | string "auto" | "auto" behaves like "system" |
| Threads | spin 1 | 1..max(1024, 4·hw_concurrency) |
| Hash | spin 16 | 1..33554432 MB |
| Clear Hash | button | |
| Ponder | check false | |
| MultiPV | spin 1 | 1..256 |
| Skill Level | spin 20 | 0..20 |
| Move Overhead | spin 10 | 0..5000 ms |
| nodestime | spin 0 | 0..10000 |
| UCI_Chess960 | check false | |
| UCI_LimitStrength | check false | |
| UCI_Elo | spin 1320 | 1320..3190 |
| UCI_ShowWDL | check false | |
| SyzygyPath | string "" | |
| SyzygyProbeDepth | spin 1 | 1..100 |
| Syzygy50MoveRule | check true | |
| SyzygyProbeLimit | spin 7 | 0..7 |
| EvalFile | string nn-1a298aa575a0.nnue | |

**Input handling:**
- Over raw UCI, an out-of-range, empty or malformed option value is **silently ignored**, and an unknown option name only prints "No such option". Validate on CCA's side or set options through python-chess `configure()`, which raises an error.
- **exit(1)** happens only on a bad position, FEN or illegal move, an unparsable `go` token (for example `wtime 1.5`), or a flip/perft error. It prints `info string CRITICAL ERROR: Command `<cmd>` failed. Reason: <msg>` first. Catch `EngineTerminatedError`, restart the engine, and re-apply options.

**WDL:**
- With `UCI_ShowWDL=true`: `info … score cp X wdl W D L …`, where W, D, L are per-mille and sum to 1000.
- Formula:
  - material = P + 3N + 3B + 5R + 9Q
  - m = clamp(material, 17, 78)/58
  - a = ((−142.72052667m + 372.35176398)m − 340.71073572)m + 415.23490212
  - b = ((5.93832785m + 15.61267078)m − 30.57816876)m + 69.63866711
  - win = 1/(1 + exp((a − v)/b)); displayed cp = round(100·v/a)
- **Every MultiPV line uses the root position's material.**
- The model is fitted to fishtest LTC self-play, so it predicts **engine-vs-engine** outcomes.
- For CCA: Q_SF = (W + 0.5·D)/1000 is suitable for the safety constraint, not for predicting human outcomes.

**Skill Level:**
- level = clamp(((37.2473e − 40.8525)e + 22.2943)e − 0.311438, 0, 19), with e = (elo − 1320)/1870.
- UCI_Elo applies only when UCI_LimitStrength is on. Skill forces MultiPV ≥ 4 and picks its move at depth 1 + level.
- It uses `static PRNG rng(now())`, so it is **non-reproducible by design**.
- It is calibrated against engines (CCRL Blitz, Stash), not humans.
- Do not use it for CCA.

**MultiPV cost:** Stockfish runs a full root search for each PV line. Restrict candidates with `analyse(..., root_moves=[...], multipv=k)` (sent as UCI `searchmoves`) rather than raising MultiPV to 256.

**Suggested config (est., benchmark with `bench` while Maia runs):**
- Threads 16–24. The CPU is hybrid, 8 P-cores + 16 E-cores / 32 threads per ARK, and Maia also needs CPU threads.
- Hash 1024–4096 MB, Move Overhead 100, UCI_ShowWDL true, NumaPolicy auto.
- For reproducible analysis: Threads=1, `go nodes N`, fixed Hash, `ucinewgame` or Clear Hash before each search, same binary and net. This is standard engine behaviour and was not source-verified.

### 4.6 python-chess (PyPI `chess` 1.11.2)

- Uploaded 2025-02-25. sdist only, so uv builds the wheel locally; pin its hash. `requires_python >=3.8`.
- `SimpleEngine.popen_uci(command, *, timeout=10.0, debug=None, setpgrp=False, **popen_args)`
- `SimpleEngine.analyse(board, limit, *, multipv=None, game=None, info=INFO_ALL, root_moves=None, options={})` returns an InfoDict, or a list of them when `multipv` is set. `info['wdl']` is a `PovWdl`.
- `MANAGED_OPTIONS`: uci_chess960, uci_variant, multipv, ponder. Setting them through `configure()` raises; pass them as call arguments instead.
- `configure({'UCI_ShowWDL': True})` must be set explicitly.
- **Do not use `PovScore.wdl()`.** Its default model 'sf' is the SF16.1 ply-based model (NormalizeToPawnValue 356), and master still has no SF17+ model.

### 4.7 lc0 (pin v0.32.1 stable, 2025-11-23)

- v0.33.0-rc0 (2026-09-05) is a pre-release, for testing only.
- Windows builds: cpu-dnnl, cpu-openblas, gpu-nvidia-cuda11/cuda12/cudnn (each also as -nodll), onnx-dml, onnx-trt. Use cuda12 for the RTX 4060.
- Search modes: classic, dag-preview, valuehead, policyhead.
- Classic-search options (identical in v0.33.0-rc0):
  - `CPuct` 1.745 [0, 100]; `CPuctBase` 38739 [1, 1e9]; `CPuctFactor` 3.894 [0, 1000].
  - cpuct(N) = CPuct + CPuctFactor·log((N + CPuctBase)/CPuctBase).
  - Pro-only (hidden but settable): `CPuctAtRoot`, `CPuctBaseAtRoot`, `CPuctFactorAtRoot`, used only when `RootHasOwnCpuctParams=true` (default false).
  - `FpuStrategy` reduction, `FpuValue` 0.330, `PolicyTemperature` 1.359 [0.1, 10], `Temperature` 0.0 (pro), `DirichletNoiseEpsilon` 0.0 (pro), `VerboseMoveStats`.
- WDL and contempt options:
  - `Contempt` (string, default ""); `ContemptMode` {play, white_side_analysis, black_side_analysis, disable}, default play; `ContemptMaxValue` 420 (pro).
  - `WDLCalibrationElo` [0, 10000], default 0; `WDLContemptAttenuation` [−10, 10], default 1.0 (pro); `WDLEvalObjectivity` [0, 1], default 1.0.
  - `WDLMaxS` 1.4 (pro); `WDLDrawRateTarget` 0.0 (pro); `WDLDrawRateReference` 0.5; `WDLBookExitBias` 0.65 (pro).
  - `DrawScore` [−1, 1], default 0; `ScoreType` WDL_mu.
  - `UCI_ShowWDL`, `UCI_ShowMovesLeft`, `UCI_Opponent`, `UCI_RatingAdv`.
- Hidden (pro-only) options are settable with `setoption`; visibility only filters listing. `--show-hidden` reveals them.
- `setoption CPuct` sent while idle takes effect at the next `go`. It cannot change mid-search. The reused tree keeps its old N/Q statistics; the pro-only `ClearTree` button, or `ucinewgame`, discards them.
- WDL contempt does not change the policy, and the lczero.org blog advises at least 10k nodes.

### 4.8 lichess-bot and Lichess BOT rules

**lichess-bot:**
- Version 2026.8.9.2, minimum Python 3.11. Requirements: chess~=1.11, PyYAML~=6.0, requests~=2.34, backoff~=2.2, rich~=15.0.
- Engine config: `engine.dir`, `engine.name` (include `.exe` on Windows), `engine.protocol: uci`, `engine.interpreter` + `interpreter_options`, `engine.uci_options` (expose CCA's λ, δ and similar here as UCI spin options), `go_commands`, `silence_stderr`, `ponder`.
- It starts the engine with `popen_uci(..., timeout=60., setpgrp=True)`.
- `config.yml.default` ships with `ponder: true`, UCI_ShowWDL true, Threads 4, Hash 512, SyzygyPath ./syzygy/, and `Move Overhead: 100` shown as an example. CCA must either implement `go ponder`, `ponderhit` and `stop` correctly, or set `ponder: false`.

**Lichess BOT account:**
- Upgrade with `POST /api/bot/account/upgrade`, OAuth scope `bot:play` (or `lichess-bot.py -u`). The account must have **played no games**, and the upgrade is **irreversible**. API spec version 2.0.174.
- BOTs play challenge games only. No pools, no UltraBullet (¼+0); 0+1 and ½+0 are allowed.
- **D:** tournament entry. The Bot tag says tournaments are off-limits, but arena creation has a `conditions.bots` field. Treat bot tournament entry as unverified.
- Rated games against humans are allowed. **U:** the "humans win or lose half rating points against bots" rule is unconfirmed as current (lila #19063 is closed with no visible resolution).
- The ToS rules on sandbagging, boosting and aborting apply to bots, and the bot must genuinely try to win. Test in casual games first.
- Fair-play grid: engines are allowed in any game played through the Bot API, and are never allowed on a human account in any real-time game. ToS last modified 2026-08-01.
- **U:** whether a BOT account may coexist with a personal account. It is at Lichess's discretion, so ask the moderators first.
- Chess.com policy: **not checked.**
- Precedent: Allie runs openly as the BOT `AllieTheChessBot`.

### 4.9 pymdp (`inferactively-pymdp` 1.0.4, 2026-08-23, MIT)

- Main API is JAX (`Agent(equinox.Module)`). The old NumPy implementation lives in `pymdp.legacy`, but installing it still pulls in JAX.
- Dependencies: jax/jaxlib ≥0.3.4,<0.11.1; equinox ≥0.9; mctx ≥0.0.5; networkx ≥3.3; opt_einsum; jaxtyping; matplotlib; seaborn; multimethod. The `[gpu]` extra is jax[cuda12].
- Native Windows: **CPU only.** The JAX platform table lists Windows NVIDIA GPU as "no" and WSL2 as "experimental".
- `Agent(A, B, C=None, D=None, E=None, pA=None, pB=None, H=None, I=None, A_dependencies=None, B_dependencies=None, B_action_dependencies=None, num_controls=None, control_fac_idx=None, policy_len=1, policies=None, gamma=1.0, alpha=1.0, …, use_utility=True, use_states_info_gain=True, use_param_info_gain=False, categorical_obs=False, action_selection='deterministic', sampling_mode='full', inference_algo='fpi', num_iter=16, batch_size=1, learning_mode='online', learn_A..E=False)`
- Loop: `qs = agent.infer_states(obs, empirical_prior=agent.D)`, then `q_pi, neg_efe = agent.infer_policies(qs)`, then `agent.sample_action(q_pi, rng_key=...)`.
- `infer_parameters(...)` returns a new Agent. Equinox modules are immutable, so reassign the result.
- Policy posterior q_pi = softmax(γ·neg_efe + log E). Agent's default γ is 1.0; `update_posterior_policies` defaults to 16.0.
- Feasible only for a small psych-state POMDP. The clock is directly observable, so feed it in as known context rather than a hidden factor.
- The first call pays a JIT compile. Warm up once per game and benchmark `infer_policies` latency.

### 4.10 open_spiel (`open-spiel` 2.0.2, 2026-08-12, Apache-2.0)

- Wheels for cp311–cp314 win_amd64. `requires_python >=3.11`. Windows docs say both "official support with pre-built wheels" and "experimental".
- Chess is registered as `"chess"` with a `chess960` parameter.
- MMD, XFP and exploitability all enumerate the full game tree (`sequence_form_utils.construct_vars`), so they **cannot run on real chess**.
- Use open_spiel only as a correctness oracle on matrix games or Kuhn poker:
  - `MMDDilatedEnt(game, alpha, stepsize=None)` has **no magnet parameter**, asserts 2-player zero-sum sequential games, and is flagged "lightly tested". Use `pyspiel.convert_to_turn_based` for matrix games.
  - ADIDAS QRE solver signatures differ between files: nonsymmetric/qre uses temperature=0.; the anneal variants use temperature=1. and exp_thresh=−1.; the symmetric variants add vr=True.
  - `XFPSolver(game, save_oracles=False)`.
  - R-NaD has been removed from master.

### 4.11 Other runtime constraints

- Allie v1: Python 3.11, torch==2.2.2, transformers==4.39.3.
- Allie v2: Python 3.9–3.12, numpy<2 (numpy 1.26.4 has no cp313 wheel), vLLM. vLLM does not support Windows natively, so this needs WSL2.
- Ailed: Python ≥3.11.

## 5. Scientific status of each C-AIME mechanism

**Status labels:**
- **EG**: empirically grounded.
- **PM**: plausible metaphor, needs validation.
- **UT**: untested hypothesis.
- **US**: unsupported.

| Mechanism | Status | Key evidence | Prediction ID |
|---|---|---|---|
| Virtual "cortisol" ODE | **PM** as a latent arousal state. **US** as cortisol. | Wrong HPA timescale (E10). The LC-NE and pupil link to *unexpected uncertainty* is EG (Yu & Dayan 2005; Preuschoff 2011; Nassar 2012). Doya 2002 is a computational mapping, not a measurement. | P2, P3 |
| Surprise driver: −ln p of the opponent's move under Maia | Quantity is **EG** (Smith & Levy 2013). Its behavioural effect in chess is **UT**. | Maia-2 is out of distribution at ≤30 s and ply <10. Values depend on the model and version. Public inference rounds to 4 d.p. | P1 |
| Time-pressure driver | **EG**, with caveats | Rapid play gives +36.5% blunders vs classical (Chabris & Hearst). PNAS 2026 links time pressure to lower quality. AKM shows a nonlinear rise below 10 s. Cüvitoğlu 2026 is a small effect (about ×1.05 at 300 cp gap and <10 s; 7 players, blitz). Time pressure makes moves *more* risk-averse (Carow & Witzig). | P3 |
| Tunnel-vision Gaussian mask | Phenomenon **EG**; Gaussian spatial form **US**; stress→Einstellung **UT**, with counter-evidence | See E13 | P4 |
| Lorenz (RK4) modulating c_puct | **US** as psychology or style. Acceptable only as a deterministic noise source. | Losada model withdrawn. No chess link. The state is unobservable, so chaos is no more unpredictable to the opponent than a keyed PRNG with the same statistics. | P5 |
| piKL KL-regularized policy | Algorithm **EG** (Jacob 2022: better human prediction and strength than imitation alone in chess and Go) | Chess gains are small: about 0.2–0.7 pp top-1 at 1500 and 0.8–2.0 pp at 1900, with 50 playouts, largest at longer time controls. Maia KDD'20: *no* search gives 5–10 pp human-likeness gains. Optimal c_puct falls as rating rises. | P7 |
| λ·H(s') "exploit" term | **UT** | Not in piKL. It trades against human-likeness. | P7 |
| WM 7±2 | **C** → K ≈ 4 | Cowan 2001; Gobet & Clarkson 2004 | — |
| Dopamine | RPE analogue **EG**; "risk-seeking / pleasure" **US** | E18 | — |
| FEP | Framework, not evidence | E19 | — |
| Style of named players (Tal, Dubov) | **US** via dynamics. Possible via data (stylometry embeddings). | McIlroy-Young 2021: 98% player identification from 100 games | P6 |

### 5.1 Required documentation labels

Put these verbatim in the README and a "Scientific status" table.

- **`arousal`** (rename from `cortisol`):
  > "Dimensionless latent state updated per ply; *inspired by, not a model of*, human arousal and stress physiology; fast dynamics loosely motivated by LC-NE and pupil-linked arousal (Yu & Dayan 2005; Aston-Jones & Cohen 2005). It does NOT model cortisol or the HPA axis (response peaks ~20–40 min after onset; Dickerson & Kemeny 2004)."
- **Surprisal:**
  > "surprisal = −ln p(move \| position, ratings) under <model id + checkpoint sha256 + time-control variant>. NOT Bayesian surprise (Itti & Baldi 2009)."
- **Attention narrowing:**
  > "Heuristic inspired by Easterbrook (1959), arousal-biased competition (Mather & Sutherland 2011) and the chess Einstellung effect (Bilalić et al. 2008); not a validated model of any of them. The Gaussian form is an engineering choice."
  Implementation: narrow on plan and candidate relatedness (sharpen the prior, top-k pruning), not on board distance.
- **Lorenz:**
  > "Deterministic chaotic noise source chosen for bounded, autocorrelated, non-periodic variation. CCA makes NO claim that human temperament, mood or any player's style (e.g. Tal, Dubov) follows chaotic dynamics; the most prominent Lorenz-emotion model was formally withdrawn (Brown, Sokal & Friedman 2013)."
  Remove all Tal/Dubov temperament language.
- **Policy:**
  > "piKL-style KL-regularized policy (Jacob et al. 2022) with CCA modifications: <list>."
  Report human-likeness and unpredictability metrics together, always.
- **WM:**
  > "capacity K, default 4 (Cowan 2001), a tunable hyperparameter, not a measured constant."
- **`rpe`:**
  > "TD-style value prediction error from evaluation changes, by analogy to Schultz, Dayan & Montague (1997)."
  No "dopamine hit" language.
- **FEP:**
  > "Terminology borrowed from information theory; CCA does not implement or test the FEP (status disputed: Colombo & Wright 2021; Bruineberg et al. 2022)."
- **Umbrella table:** for each mechanism, give its status (EG/PM/UT/US), its test ID (P1–P9) and its result (pending, passed or failed).

### 5.2 Falsifiable predictions

**Statistical design for all predictions:**
- Pre-register every test.
- Human data: mixed-effects models with player random effects. Moves are clustered within players.
- Engine A/B: SPRT (cutechess or fastchess).
- The lab stress effect d ≈ 0.17 would need about 540 subjects per arm at 80% power and α = .05 (derived, between-subject). Do not treat that as a game count.

| ID | Test | Kill criterion |
|---|---|---|
| **P1** Surprise→behaviour | On Lichess CC0 games with %clk, regress the reply's think time and its win-probability loss on the Maia surprisal of the opponent's move. Controls: Stockfish eval, Maia policy entropy, top-2 eval gap, remaining clock, ratings, player effects. | The surprisal coefficient's 95% CI includes 0 at adequate power. Then remove the surprise→arousal path, or relabel it as pure design. |
| **P2** Arousal ODE | With arousal on, human-move NLL and top-1 must improve over Maia alone, on plies after high-surprise moves and in low-clock positions. Ablations: arousal off; arousal series shuffled across games; a "just weaker" Maia at a lower bin. Fit the decay half-life in plies. | No gain over all ablations, or the best-fit half-life goes to 0. Then drop the ODE and use an instantaneous feature. |
| **P3** Risk direction | In human data, low clock should predict risk-averse moves, and a recent negative eval swing should predict risk-seeking moves. CCA must reproduce both signs. | One scalar cannot produce both. Then split it into `clock_pressure` and `recent_loss_signal`. |
| **P4** Narrowing | Under low clock, the realized choice entropy relative to Maia's policy entropy should fall (the stress→habit shift, Schwabe & Wolf 2009). CCA with the mask must match this curve better than without it. On two-solution Einstellung positions, CCA's pattern should match the human one and weaken with rating. | The mask gives no improvement in fit. Remove it. |
| **P5** Lorenz | At equal Elo, compare (A) Lorenz, (B) an IAAFT phase-randomized surrogate of the same series, and (C) an OU process with matched ACF. Metric: opponent-side predictability, i.e. Maia and Stockfish top-1 agreement and NLL on CCA's moves. Also expected score. | A is not significantly better than B and C. Replace it with PRNG+OU. |
| **P6** Style | If CCA claims a named style, a stylometry model or a per-player fine-tuned Maia must place CCA's games closer to that player than to baseline Maia at the same rating. | Otherwise withdraw the claim. |
| **P7** H(s') / exploit term | At matched objective soundness (rate of Stockfish expected-score drops > 0.1), with and without the term: measure opponent eval loss against Maia-k opponents (1100–1900), then on the BOT account; also human-likeness. | No gain in opponent error at matched soundness. Delete the term. |
| **P8** Human-aware expectimax (§7 #2) | Against the baselines in §7 Gate 0, at matched soundness: expected score against Maia-k, then against humans on the BOT account. | No advantage over Lc0 WDL-contempt and the Hamade 2-ply Expector. |
| **P9** Timing model | Held-out NLL. Pearson r against Allie's 0.697. Per-phase KS and Wasserstein distances. Autocorrelation at lags 1–5, own and opponent. Share of budget used by move 40 (Sigman 3+0: 74.7–77.9%). Flag rate. | Worse than Allie's point estimate, or it flags more often than humans. |

## 6. Chaos numerics (Module 2)

System: Lorenz with σ = 10, ρ = 28, β = 8/3. All values are computed unless noted. Where the verifier re-ran a computation, the table gives its numbers.

### 6.1 Computed values

| Quantity | Value |
|---|---|
| Largest Lyapunov exponent λ1 | 0.9059 (Benettin; researcher and verifier agree). 0.904–0.907 by tangent-linear + QR. Literature: 0.906 (Sprott, RK4 h=0.001, 1e9 steps) — https://sprott.physics.wisc.edu/chaos/lorenzle.htm |
| Lyapunov spectrum | (0.905, ≈0, −14.570). Sum −13.6667 = −(σ + 1 + β), as expected. D_KY = 2.062 (Sprott). |
| z on the attractor | z̄ = **23.55**, σ_z = **8.62**. Skew +0.21, excess kurtosis −0.86. Percentiles 1/5/50/95/99 = 7.2 / 10.7 / 22.4 / 38.0 / 41.4. The range is a sample extreme; do not hard-code it. |
| x and y | σ_x = **7.92**, mean x ≈ 0; σ_y = 9.01 |
| RK4 stability at dt = 0.01 | h·max\|eig J\| = 0.21–0.23, far below the RK4 limit of 2.785 |
| RK4 accuracy at dt = 0.01 | One-step error median ~4–5e-7, max 3.8e-5. Invariant statistics match dt = 0.005 to within 0.004. dt = 0.05 is biased (mean z 23.49). Trajectories stay faithful for ~11 time units. RK4 global error is O(h^4), so halving dt buys ~ln(16)/λ ≈ 3.1 t.u. of fidelity. |
| Autocorrelation of z | Phase-coherent, dominant period ~0.76 t.u. (~76 steps). ACF first drops below 1/e at 14 steps and first crosses 0 at 20. Envelope: 0.48 (lags 100–200), 0.35 (500–600), 0.21 (1000–1100), 0.08 (2000–2100). |
| corr(z_k, z_{k+K}) | K = 10: .63 · 50: −.38 · 76: .56 · 100: −.23 · 153: .46 · 200: −.32 · 300: .39 · 500: −.30 · 1000: .09 · 2000: −.06 · 3000: −.03 |
| corr(x_k, x_{k+K}) | K = 100: .12 · 200: .05 · 300: .036 · 500: .007 · 1000: .001. τ_int ≈ 96–98 steps. Lobe dwell: median 153 steps. |
| u = tanh((z − z̄)/σ_z) | **U-shaped and bimodal**: mean −0.024, sd 0.660, excess kurtosis −1.51, bimodality coefficient 0.684. P(\|u\| > 0.75) = 0.39, P(\|u\| > 0.9) = 0.14. In practice it acts like a noisy two-state switch. |
| c/c_base = 1 + λ_chaos·u, with λ_chaos = 0.25 | Range [0.753, 1.248], 5–95% [0.774, 1.233], mean 0.994. c stays positive only if λ_chaos < 1.011. |
| Burn-in from a hashed initial condition | **At least 3000 steps**, 5000 to be safe. At 3000 steps the KS distance is 0.014–0.016 against a critical value of 0.022. The researcher's "1000 steps" is superseded: the verifier compared against the true invariant measure, where the researcher compared against a 3000-step ensemble. |
| Surprise kicks y += k·S | Bounded: max\|state\| = 47.6, 48.9, 52.6, 69.9, 140.9 for k = 0, 0.5, 1, 3, 10. **No directional effect**: corr(S, Δu) ≤ 0.05. The invariant measure distorts as k grows. |
| Modulating ρ (unsafe) | Stable fixed point at ρ = 20. Bistable around 24.5. Periodic windows at ρ ≈ 99.65, 100.5, 150, 160, 220, 350. |
| Alternatives | Rössler λ1 ≈ 0.070 (13× slower mixing). Logistic map at r = 4: λ = ln 2, but it degenerates in float after ~10^7 iterations. Tent map collapses to 1.0 after 53–55 iterations; never use it in binary floating point. |
| Cost per step | Float, pure Python: 0.67–0.77 µs. Fixed-point Q24.40: 2.7–3.1 µs. |

### 6.2 Reproducibility facts

- **Golden value:** from (1, 1, 1), h = 0.01, 10k steps, z = **10.659565937310285** (`0x1.551b2a0649b45p+3`). This holds **only** for the literal source form `x + h/2*k` and `x + h/6*(k1 + 2*k2 + 2*k3 + k4)`. The mathematically equal form `0.5*h*k … h*(…)/6` gives **7.739676351181291**. The CI test must therefore pin the exact source text, not just "RK4".
- **What breaks bit-identity** (first difference / \|dz\| > 1e-6 / \|dz\| > 1):

  | Change | Onset |
  |---|---|
  | Equivalent reordering | step 46 / 2841 / 4419 |
  | FMA contraction | steps 11–134 / ~2837 / ~4265 |
  | `sum()` (algorithm changed in Python 3.12) | step 2–4 / — / ~4264 |
  | float32 | step 1 / 20 / 1856 |

  Also: `np.tanh` and `math.tanh` differ by 1 ULP on 21.7% of inputs.
- **IEEE-754 guarantee:** only +, −, ×, ÷, sqrt, remainder and int↔float conversion are correctly rounded (Goldberg 1991). Transcendental functions and CPython's `**` (which calls libm pow) are platform-dependent.
- **Compiler traps:** GCC defaults to `-ffp-contract=fast` outside strict ISO mode. Clang defaults to `-ffp-contract=on`, so extensions built with clang or clang-cl on an FMA3 CPU can fuse multiply-adds.
- **NumPy RNG:** streams are guaranteed only for the same build on the same machine.
- **Measured vs inferred:** bit-identity across OS, CPU or Python versions was **inferred, not measured**, for the float path.

### 6.3 Reproducibility recipe

1. **Tier A (recommended): fixed-point integer Lorenz.**
   - Q24.40 Python ints with floor shifts; β·z computed as `(8*z)//3`; H = `2**40//100`.
   - Checks: mean z 23.55, sd 8.62, λ1 ≈ 0.909.
   - Bit-identical on any machine by construction, until the value is converted to float.
2. **Tier B: scalar float64, pure Python.**
   - Frozen expression order; constants written as literals.
   - **Banned inside the integrator:** `sum`, `math.fsum`, `math.fma`, `np.dot`, `@`, `**`, float32, and numba/Cython/C/fastmath code paths.
   - CI golden test: compare the exact float hex on every supported OS, CPU and Python version.
3. **Anchoring:**
   - Initial condition = 3 ints or doubles taken from **HMAC-SHA256(secret_key, game_id)**, then burn in ≥3000 steps.
   - Optionally re-anchor every N plies.
   - **The seed must stay secret.** CCA is open source, so a seed or state logged in the PGN lets any viewer replay the whole modulation. Publish a hash commitment and reveal the seed after the game.
4. **Choosing K (steps per move):**
   - For independent per-move values: use **x with K ≥ 500**, or z with K ≥ 3000 (at K = 2000, z still shows corr −0.06).
   - For deliberate "mood persistence": K = 20–40, declared as a design parameter.
   - Avoid K near multiples of 76 when using z.
5. **Output mapping:** do not use libm tanh. Use the algebraic sigmoid v/√(1 + v²), which needs only correctly rounded operations, or quantize to a 2^-20 grid. For a flat marginal distribution, use a probability-integral transform through a frozen CDF table.
6. **Coupling:**
   - Only use state kicks y += k·clip(S_q, 0, S_max), with S_q = round(−log2 P·16)/16 and k·S_max ≤ ~0.5·σ_y (≈ 4.5; for example k = 0.45 with S_max = 10 bits).
   - **Never modulate ρ, σ or β.**
   - Any intended *directional* effect of surprise or time goes into an explicit term: log λ_t = log λ_0 + κ_c·u_t + κ_S·g(S) + κ_t·h(t_left).
7. **Replay log:** record the seed commitment, game_id, K, dt, code version, quantized S_q, Maia checkpoint sha256, model type and Elo inputs. For Stockfish also record the binary and net hashes, Threads, Hash and node counts.

### 6.4 What to modulate when the backend is Stockfish

Listed in order of preference.

1. **piKL λ**, multiplicatively in log space: λ_t = λ_0·exp(κ·u), with κ ≤ ln 2, so λ_t stays within [λ_0/2, 2λ_0]. This is the dial between human-like and engine-like play.
2. **Sampling temperature T** over the safety set.
3. **Exploitation weight** on the opponent reply model, or the confidence p in §7.
4. **Safety tolerance δ.** Only narrow it; the budget rule caps it.
5. **Search budget** (`go nodes` or `movetime`). Tie it to the timing model rather than to chaos.
6. **MultiPV breadth** in {2..8}, keeping in mind the depth cost.

Never modulate Skill Level or UCI_Elo: they are non-reproducible and add uncontrolled randomness.

If an MCTS backend is added (lc0, or CCA's own PUCT over Maia priors):
- Apply c(t) to lc0 `CPuct` (default 1.745) through `setoption` between `go` commands.
- Keep λ_chaos ≤ 0.5.
- Remember that λ_N = c·√N/(\|A\| + N).
- Decide deliberately between tree reuse and `ClearTree`.

## 7. Recommended architecture upgrades (ranked by expected real impact)

### Gate 0 (prerequisite): evaluation harness

Nothing below is claimed until it passes this harness.

- **Baselines:**
  - plain Maia at the target Elo;
  - Stockfish with UCI_LimitStrength (floor 1320);
  - Lc0 v0.32.1 with ContemptMode=play, WDLCalibrationElo and Contempt set to the Elo difference;
  - a Hamade-style 2-ply Expector;
  - an Ailed-style psyche modulation.
- **Metrics:**
  - expected score against Maia-k (1100–1900), then against humans on the BOT account;
  - move-match against Maia at the target Elo;
  - opponent-side log-loss on CCA's moves (unpredictability);
  - objective blunder rate (Stockfish expected-score drop > 0.1).
- **Statistics:** SPRT for engine tests; mixed-effects models for human data.

### Ranked upgrades

| Rank | Upgrade | Justification (verified source) | Cost and caveats |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | **Canonical piKL over a Stockfish safety set.** π(c) ∝ τ(c)^{1/T}·exp(U(c)/λ) over S = {c : E_SF(c) ≥ E_SF(best) − δ_t}. τ is Maia's masked log-softmax at CCA's target Elo, taken from logits, not the rounded API. U starts as E_SF = (W + D/2)/1000 and is upgraded by #2. λ is set per rating bucket: the optimal c_puct fell as rating rose (piKL), and Maia-2 saturates at ≥2000. Sample with a seeded counter-based PRNG and an entropy floor. | Jacob 2022 (Maia anchor improves human prediction and strength). Sokota 2023: with q held fixed, the MMD Eq. 12 fixed point is π ∝ ρ·exp(q/α), i.e. the piKL form with ρ = Maia (derived). Transcendence 2024: temperature trades human-likeness against strength. | Low cost. Expect small gains in human-likeness (0.2–2 pp in piKL). Put λ in expected-score units (est. starting grid λ ∈ {0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2}). |
| **2** | **Human-aware expectimax.** For each c in S, get the opponent's reply distribution p_h(r \| s_c, elo_self = opponent, elo_oppo = CCA) and keep the top-R replies covering ~95% of the mass. U(c) = Σ_r p_h(r)·V_h(s_c, r), with V_h human-calibrated: the Maia-3 WDL head, a calibrated Maia value, or Lc0 WDLCalibrationElo. Optionally run a shallow Stockfish check at the leaf to catch refutations. Trap value T(c) = U(c) − E_SF(c). | Hamade 2024: the Expector was the best agent (66.5% win-share), but in collaborative play against Maia bots only. Lc0 WDL-contempt is the mature baseline. Lc0 knight-odds nets went +14 =2 −2 against a GM (n = 18, anecdotal). L-IBM 2024: human play fits bounded search budgets. | This is the only mechanism aimed directly at "exploit", but there is **no controlled test against humans**. Est. cost: K = 6 × R = 6 = 36 leaves per move; Maia leaves fit in one GPU batch; Stockfish leaf checks at 0.1–0.3 s each give ~4–11 s/move single-stream. Parallelize Stockfish, or score leaves with V_h only at blitz. Maia-3 in-process means AGPL. |
| **3** | **Exploitation safety budget.** Keep a heuristic budget k_t in expected-score units, updated RWYWE-style with expected (not realized) gains, and cap δ_t ≤ min(k_t, δ_max). Expose one confidence knob p, Johanson-style, and sweep it to plot exploitation against exploitability. | Ganzfried & Sandholm 2015 (RWYWE is safe; RWYW is not). Johanson 2007: the frontier is highly concave, so large cuts in exploitability cost little exploitation. Hamade: over-aggressive exploitation backfires with a mismatched model. | **No formal guarantee** in chess: the game value is unknown and the Stockfish eval is not a payoff. The per-move blend p·V_model + (1 − p)·V_SF is only a 1-ply heuristic analogue of RNR. |
| **4** | **Position difficulty as the primary error signal.** Per-candidate features: Maia policy entropy at the opponent's Elo; top-2 eval gap ln(1 + d); value of computation √ΔUC (Stockfish depth 1 vs deep); Guid–Bratko complexity from iterative deepening with MultiPV = 2, depth range recalibrated for SF19; weak-vs-strong engine gap; fragility score; optionally a puzzle-difficulty regressor as one feature. | AKM 2016 (difficulty > skill and time, in tablebase positions). Sunde (gap coefficient −0.92, single-regressor column). Russek 2025 (√ΔUC, steeper for stronger players). Zaidi & Guerzhoy 2024 (non-obviousness). Barthelemy 2025. | Cheap. Difficulty dominance in middlegames is unproven. Puzzle-difficulty labels have domain shift, since solvers know a tactic exists. |
| **5** | **Candidate generation:** Maia top-k ∪ Stockfish best → `analyse(root_moves=…, multipv=k)`, instead of a very large MultiPV. | sf_19 search.cpp: "full root search for each PV line" | Better Q per candidate at a fixed time budget. |
| **6** | **Regime handling for Maia's blind spots.** Plies 1–10: opening book or Stockfish-only policy (Maia-2 excluded these plies, and issues #4, #5, #13 show pathologies). Clock ≤30 s: treat Maia-2 probabilities and surprise as out of distribution; damp exploitation or switch to a validated time-aware model. Optional book of engine-equal, human-unequal positions filtered by opponent Elo band. | Maia-2 training filters (`main.py`). Park 2026 (replicated, but the median skew is only about 1.8 pp; observational; unreviewed). | Low cost. Expect little from the book alone. |
| **7** | **Clock-aware timing model**, replacing any copied constants. T = δ_floor + F·X_fast + (1 − F)·X_slow. F is a hurdle for recaptures, forced moves, book, previous fast move and ln(R). ln X_slow ~ N(μ, σ²) with μ = θ_{elo,tc} + τ_player + spline(ply) + b_B·ln(budget) + b_V·√ΔUC − b_G·ln(1 + gap) + b_H·H_maia + AR terms (own and opponent residuals) + an explicit budget term (Sigman found *negative* long-range correlations). σ = σ_0·exp(s_1·(Elo − 1500)/400). Constraint: T ≤ κ(R)·R. Fit on Lichess CC0 with a convolution likelihood over (d − 1, d + 1): the difference of two 1-s clocks has a triangular error, so P(k ≤ T < k + 1) is misspecified. The fast component needs centisecond API clocks. Compare against ex-Gaussian and shifted-Wald alternatives by held-out NLL. Feed t̂ to the search budget (N_sim = ⌊c·t̂⌋, Allie). | Sigman 2010. Sunde (joint-model coefficients 0.0947 / 0.0193 / −0.8294; elite classical players; first 15 moves excluded). Russek 2025. Allie (r = 0.697 as a point estimate). van der Linden 2006. Heathcote 1991. Anders 2016. | Sigman's across-game dispersion is an unconditional ceiling (σ = √ln(1 + b²) = 0.78 for b = 0.91 and **1.02** for b = 1.36). The conditional σ must be fitted. Collecting API data is rate-limited (one request at a time; wait 1 min after a 429). Chess.com's "0.1 s per premove" is **U**. |
| **8** | **Split the arousal state** into `clock_pressure` and `recent_loss_signal`. Drive them from a TD-style `rpe` and surprisal, with a fitted decay. | Carow & Witzig 2025 found opposite risk signs for these two conditions. Schwabe & Wolf 2009. | Gated by P1–P3. |
| **9** | **Style switching per game or phase** via style embeddings (Maia4All after ~20 games; champion embeddings on Maia-2; Mixture-of-Masters-style routing). This also defeats stylometry aimed at CCA itself. | Maia4All (TMLR 2026). Stylometry (NeurIPS 2021). The routing and embedding papers are 2026 preprints. | Maia4All is work in progress. Preprint licenses are **U**. |
| **10** | **Regan–Haworth opponent-precision estimator.** y = exp(−(δ/s)^c), p_i = p_0^{1/y_i}. Online MLE of s gives an "effective Elo" observation for the arousal layer and cross-checks Maia surprise. | Regan & Haworth 2011 | Refit on modern Stockfish plus Lichess data. The original fit used Rybka 3 at depth 13. The paper is internally inconsistent: it uses both plain normalization and the p_0^{1/y} conversion, the grid does not contain the reported c, and δ units are unconfirmed. Pick one convention and document it. |
| **11** | **Demote Lorenz** to optional gated noise per §6. Default to PRNG + OU with matched marginal and ACF. | §6 plus P5 | Removes a reproducibility hazard. |
| **12** | **Optional pymdp psych-state POMDP** (about 9 states, 4 control modes, policy_len ≤ 2). The clock is observed context. The info-gain term formalizes "probing" moves. | pymdp 1.0.4; Heins 2022 | Low expected impact. JIT latency must be benchmarked. |

## 8. Open risks

| Risk | Severity | Mitigation / next action |
|---|---|---|
| Ethics and ToS: a system framed as "exploiting human cognitive weaknesses" | High | Deploy only on a fresh, declared Lichess BOT account (irreversible upgrade; challenges only; genuinely trying to win; no sandbagging). Never assist a human account. Get moderator approval for a second account. Obtain informed consent and an IRB-style review for any human-subject evaluation; prefer offline CC0 data. Chess.com rules unchecked. Nothing may be tuned against anti-cheat detection. |
| License contagion | High | python-chess is GPL, so choose GPL-3.0-or-later now. Maia-3 in-process means AGPL-3.0 for a hosted bot. Maia-2 and Maia-3 weight licenses are unknown, so do not rehost the weights. Get a lawyer's review before any commercial use. |
| Maia-2 out of distribution exactly where C-AIME acts (≤30 s, ply <10, no history, coarse Elo, rapid only in the paper) | High | Regime switching (§7 #6), validation at low clock, or fine-tuning on low-clock positions. Evaluate Maia-3 (continuous Elo, history), keeping in mind it has no clock input either. |
| Install blockers: maia2 <3.13; CPU-only PyPI torch on Windows; maia3 not on PyPI; vLLM not native on Windows | High | Py3.12 uv environment with an explicit cu128 torch index (§4.1). Pin the maia3 commit and the HF revisions. |
| Evidence strength behind exploitation | High | Hamade is collaborative play against bots; Matilda shows gains only above 3000 Elo (below 2500 it just preserves Maia-3); the Lc0 odds result is n = 18 at knight odds; Park is ~1.8 pp; piKL gains are 0.2–2 pp. Treat every design claim as a hypothesis and use pre-registered tests P7–P8. |
| Small human effect sizes and clustering | Medium | Power analysis with design effects. Mixed-effects models. No post-hoc tuning. |
| Unreviewed 2026 preprints (Matilda, Otter, ChessMimic, Park, Ailed, MoM, UniMaia, Sogliuzzo) | Medium | Replicate in the CCA harness before they drive design. Their test sets differ, so accuracy numbers cannot be compared with each other. |
| Numerical traps: rounding to 4 d.p. breaks −ln p; fp16 AMP in Maia-3; Maia-2's value output is uncalibrated and White-perspective | Medium | Use the logits adapter with an epsilon floor. Calibrate V_h. Disable AMP for log-prob computation if needed (effect untested). |
